extractor.prompt: Extract foundational structures and founding relations in Henry's phenomenology of manifestation, focusing on how higher-order objectivities emerge through immanent self-relation rather than transcendent constitution.
extractor.note: Partial extraction covering §§37 and 42-43. Henry distinguishes between transcendent founding (where freedom projects horizons) and immanent founding (where life receives itself). Untouched: §§54-57 on affectivity, §§31-36 on transcendence/immanence contrast, sections on embodiment and concrete manifestation.

coverage_note: Covers Henry's account of the structural difference between 'a situation' (pragmatic, transcendently founded) and 'being-in-situation' (ontologically founding, impossible to found from transcendence). Also covers the internal structure of immanence as the exclusion of horizonal constitution and the self-receiving character of life. Partially read: dense material on Heidegger's Nichtigkeit, the role of affectivity, and Henry's critique of freedom; unread: Sections II and IV material on concrete manifestation and affective tonalities.

units.claim: Situation structurally bifurcates: transcendence founds particular pragmatic situations but not the structural fact of being-situated, which is imposed on transcendence from outside itself.
units.quote: In investment, transcendence founds each time *a situation*, not *the fact for it of finding itself in this situation*. In this fact, however, resides the essence of situation — *not in the situation itself, but in the fact of finding oneself thus in the situation*, in such a way that this coming does not depend on transcendence but is imposed on it.

units.claim: The internal structure of immanence excludes transcendence ontologically: no opposition, representation, distance, or division exists in the essence; the absence of transcendence is the essence's own internal nature.
units.quote: *It is in the essence itself that there is nothing transcendent; it is in the essence — in its internal nature — that the thought of exclusion penetrates.* *In the essence itself, there is nothing exterior, nothing foreign*.

units.claim: Life is the unity of receiver and received: to be oneself what one receives, with receiver and received identical in immediate self-presence, constitutes the immanent structure founding all objectivities.
units.quote: They do not *become* it; *they are it* — and that since always, because, since always, this is what they are — what they receive insofar precisely as *they are themselves what they receive*.
